02 / THE PROBLEM

There are two ways software usually wastes your time.

Your software is slowing you down.

The product exists, but something isn't working. Delivery has slowed, a migration is stuck, technical debt is getting expensive, or nobody owns the difficult decisions.

I step in, own the problem, and fix it.

Migrations · architecture · product rescue · technical debt · performance · senior ownership

The process is slowing you down.

Your team has built a workflow around spreadsheets, email, copy/paste, and disconnected tools. It works — because people spend hours keeping it alive.

I figure out what shouldn't require a person, and build the system that removes it.

Internal software · workflow apps · integrations · dashboards · automation

05 / APPROACH

Don't automate the mess.

The first step isn't writing code. Start with the problem, not the technology.

1 — Understand

I work with the people actually doing the work.

2 — Simplify

A bad process automated is still a bad process.

The smallest system that solves the real problem.

4 — Leave it better

Something your team can actually maintain.

06 / EXISTING SOFTWARE

When the problem is already inside the codebase.

You don't always need new software. Sometimes you need someone senior enough to understand what is actually wrong and take responsibility for fixing it.

Rescue

A critical project is stuck and progress is slowing. Someone needs to take ownership.

Migration

A risky migration needs someone who understands both the existing system and where it needs to go.

Cleanup

Technical debt is no longer just an engineering concern. It is making the business slower.

Senior gap

Good developers, but nobody making the difficult technical decisions and owning them across the system.
